ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: If grass went extinct, what organism would be most affected?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The diagram is a food web. Grass is labeled Producer on the left. Arrows go from Grass to Mouse labeled Primary Consumer and from Grass to Deer labeled Primary Consumer. Mouse leads to Snake labeled Secondary Consumer, then to Eagle labeled Tertiary Consumer. Deer leads to Wolf labeled Secondary Consumer, and Wolf leads toward Fungus labeled Decomposer; there is also a red downward arrow from the Eagle area toward the lower part of the web. Reasoning: If grass went extinct, organisms that eat grass directly would be affected first because they would lose their immediate food source. The diagram shows Mouse as a direct primary consumer of grass, so Mouse would be immediately affected. The diagram also shows Deer as another direct primary consumer, so the direct-effect evidence is somewhat shared, but Mouse is a supported direct-consumer answer. Answer: Mouse.
